deep-research.title: Break the ice
talkingPoints: To do or say something to relieve tension or get conversation started, especially among strangers.
She told a joke to break the ice at the start of the meeting.
Describe a time you had to break the ice with someone you'd just met.

deep-research.title: Better late than never
talkingPoints: It is better for something to happen or arrive late than not at all.
He finally apologized after two years — better late than never.
Describe a time you finished or said something late, but it was still better late than never.

deep-research.title: Get a taste of your own medicine
talkingPoints: To be treated the way you have treated others, especially when it is unpleasant.
The prankster finally got a taste of his own medicine when his friends pranked him back.
Share a time you got a taste of your own medicine after treating someone a certain way.

deep-research.title: Play devil's advocate
talkingPoints: To argue against something you may actually agree with, in order to spark debate or test an idea.
I'll play devil's advocate here: what if the plan fails because of the cost?
Talk about a time you played devil's advocate in a discussion, or wish you had.

deep-research.title: Sweep under the rug
talkingPoints: To hide or ignore a problem instead of dealing with it.
The company tried to sweep the safety complaints under the rug.
Share a time an issue was swept under the rug instead of being properly addressed.

deep-research.title: A leopard can't change its spots
talkingPoints: A person's basic character or nature does not change, even if they try to appear different.
He promised to be more honest this time, but a leopard can't change its spots.
Describe a time you saw that a leopard can't change its spots, in yourself or someone else.

deep-research.title: Kindness
talkingPoints: The quality of being friendly, generous, and considerate toward others.
A small act of kindness from a stranger brightened her whole day.
Share a time someone's kindness caught you off guard and changed your mood.

deep-research.title: Home
talkingPoints: The place where one lives, or a feeling of belonging and comfort.
No matter where she traveled, this small apartment always felt like home.
Describe what makes a place feel like home to you.

deep-research.title: Compassion
talkingPoints: Sympathetic concern for the suffering of others, paired with a desire to help.
Her compassion for the injured bird surprised everyone on the hike.
Describe a moment someone's compassion toward you made a real difference.

deep-research.title: Effort
talkingPoints: The physical or mental energy exerted to achieve something.
It took real effort to stay calm during the negotiation.
Talk about something that required far more effort than you expected.

deep-research.title: Childhood
talkingPoints: The period of a person's life from birth until they reach adulthood.
His childhood in a small fishing village shaped his love of the sea.
Share a childhood memory that still influences who you are today.

deep-research.title: Surprise
talkingPoints: An unexpected or astonishing event.
The surprise party left him speechless for the first time in his life.
Describe a surprise, good or bad, that you never saw coming.

deep-research.title: Authenticity
talkingPoints: The quality of being genuine and true to one's own character rather than a copy or imitation.
His authenticity on stage made the audience feel like they were talking to a friend.
Talk about a time you dropped a persona and let people see who you really are.

deep-research.title: Transition
talkingPoints: The process of changing from one state or condition to another.
The transition from student to full-time employee was harder than she expected.
Describe a major transition in your life and what helped you get through it.

deep-research.title: Competition
talkingPoints: The activity or condition of striving to gain or win something by defeating others.
Friendly competition between the two branches pushed both sales teams to new records.
Describe how competition, healthy or not, has shaped one of your biggest achievements.

deep-research.title: Nostalgia
talkingPoints: A sentimental longing for the past.
The smell of the old bakery filled him with nostalgia for summers at his grandmother's.
Describe a specific memory that fills you with nostalgia and why it still matters to you.

deep-research.title: Solidarity
talkingPoints: Unity or agreement of feeling or action among a group with a common interest.
The workers' solidarity during the strike kept morale high even after weeks without pay.
Talk about a moment you felt real solidarity with a group of strangers or coworkers.

deep-research.title: Commitment
talkingPoints: The state of being dedicated to a cause, activity, or relationship.
Her commitment to the team never wavered, even during the season they lost every game.
Describe a commitment you've kept even when it got hard to keep.

deep-research.title: Utilitarianism
talkingPoints: An ethical theory holding that the best action is the one that produces the greatest good for the greatest number.
The city council used utilitarianism to justify a policy that benefited the majority at a small cost to a few.
Describe a real decision where following utilitarianism would mean sacrificing the interests of a minority, and say whether you'd still choose it.

deep-research.title: Dialectic
talkingPoints: A method of reasoning that resolves conflict between opposing ideas by combining them into a more complete understanding.
Through dialectic, the two debaters found that their opposing arguments both contained part of the truth.
Walk through a disagreement you've had, treating it as a dialectic, and explain what a synthesis of both sides might look like.

deep-research.title: Narrative
talkingPoints: A story or connected account used to explain or make sense of events.
The company changed its public narrative after the scandal to focus on reform.
Reflect on the personal narrative you tell yourself about your own life, and whether it's still serving you well.

deep-research.title: Memory
talkingPoints: The mental capacity to store, retain, and recall information and past experiences.
Her memory of the accident was hazy, but the fear it left behind was vivid.
Share a memory you're not sure is entirely accurate anymore, and discuss how memory can change over time.

deep-research.title: Systems
talkingPoints: Sets of interconnected parts that function together as a whole.
Engineers study how small failures in complex systems can cascade into major breakdowns.
Describe a system in your own life, whether a routine, a workplace, or a relationship, and how one small change affected the whole.

deep-research.title: Compassion fatigue
talkingPoints: Emotional exhaustion caused by prolonged exposure to others' suffering, common among caregivers and helping professionals.
After years in the emergency room, the nurse recognized the early signs of compassion fatigue in herself.
Discuss a time you experienced compassion fatigue, whether caring for a person, a cause, or the news, and how you recovered.

general.title: Hit the nail on the head
talkingPoints: To describe exactly what is causing a situation or problem; to be exactly right.
When she said the project failed due to poor planning, she hit the nail on the head.
Talk about a time someone hit the nail on the head about a problem you were facing.

general.title: A blessing in disguise
talkingPoints: Something that seems bad or unlucky at first but turns out to have a good result.
Getting laid off was a blessing in disguise because it pushed me to start my own business.
Share a setback in your life that turned out to be a blessing in disguise.

general.title: Have a lot on your plate
talkingPoints: To have many tasks or responsibilities to deal with at once.
I can't take on another project right now — I already have a lot on my plate.
Describe a period in your life when you had a lot on your plate and how you coped.

general.title: Face the music
talkingPoints: To accept and deal with the unpleasant consequences of your actions.
After skipping the meeting, he had to face the music with his boss.
Share a time you had to face the music after making a mistake.

general.title: Throw someone under the bus
talkingPoints: To betray someone for personal gain.
He threw his teammate under the bus to save his own reputation.
Share a time you were thrown under the bus and how it changed the way you trust at work.

general.title: Separate the wheat from the chaff
talkingPoints: To distinguish what is valuable or useful from what is worthless.
The first round of interviews helped us separate the wheat from the chaff among applicants.
Share a process you used to separate the wheat from the chaff when making a big decision.

general.title: Hope
talkingPoints: A feeling of expectation and desire for a certain thing to happen.
Even in the hospital, she never lost hope that things would get better.
Talk about a time you held onto hope even when the odds seemed against you.

general.title: Dream
talkingPoints: A cherished hope, ambition, or aspiration; also images experienced during sleep.
Becoming a doctor had been her dream since childhood.
Talk about a dream you're still chasing and what's stopping you.

general.title: Empathy
talkingPoints: The ability to understand and share the feelings of another person.
His empathy for the new employee helped her settle in faster.
Share a time you truly put yourself in someone else's shoes.

general.title: Kindness
talkingPoints: The quality of being friendly, generous, and considerate toward others.
A small act of kindness from a stranger brightened her whole day.
Share a time someone's kindness caught you off guard and changed your mood.

general.title: Friendship
talkingPoints: A close relationship of mutual affection and trust between people.
Their friendship survived twenty years and three different countries.
Describe a friendship that has shaped who you are today.

general.title: Comfort
talkingPoints: A state of physical ease or a feeling of relief from distress.
Her mother's voice on the phone was all the comfort she needed that night.
Talk about what gives you comfort during a hard week.

general.title: Vulnerability
talkingPoints: The state of being open to emotional exposure or harm.
Admitting she was scared took real vulnerability in front of her whole team.
Share a moment when being vulnerable with someone actually strengthened the relationship.

general.title: Challenge
talkingPoints: A task or situation that tests someone's abilities.
Learning a new language later in life was the biggest challenge he'd taken on in years.
Talk about a challenge you didn't think you'd get through, and how you did.

general.title: Cooperation
talkingPoints: The process of working together toward the same end.
Cooperation between rival unions was rare, but it saved both companies from closing.
Share a time cooperating with someone you disagreed with led to a better outcome.

general.title: Perspective
talkingPoints: A particular attitude toward or way of regarding something.
Traveling alone for a month completely changed her perspective on what she needed to be happy.
Talk about an experience that gave you a completely new perspective on your own life.

general.title: Tolerance
talkingPoints: The ability or willingness to accept beliefs or behavior different from one's own.
Growing up in a mixed neighborhood taught her a kind of tolerance textbooks never could.
Describe an experience that stretched your tolerance for a viewpoint very different from your own.

general.title: Doubt
talkingPoints: A feeling of uncertainty about the truth or reliability of something.
Doubt crept in the night before the exam, even after months of preparation.
Talk about a moment of real doubt and how you pushed through it, or didn't.

general.title: Virtue ethics
talkingPoints: An ethical approach that focuses on the character and virtues of the person acting rather than rules or consequences.
Instead of asking what rule applied, she used virtue ethics and asked what a courageous person would do.
Identify one virtue you're actively trying to cultivate in yourself and explain why you chose that one over others.

general.title: Sovereignty
talkingPoints: The authority of a state or individual to govern itself without outside interference.
The treaty was controversial because critics felt it undermined national sovereignty.
Discuss where you think the line should be drawn between respecting a nation's sovereignty and intervening to prevent harm.

general.title: Discourse
talkingPoints: Communication, especially formal or extended discussion, about a particular topic.
Public discourse around climate change has shifted dramatically over the past decade.
Discuss how you think public discourse on a topic you care about could become more productive.

general.title: Trauma
talkingPoints: A deeply distressing or disturbing experience that has a lasting psychological impact.
Years after the accident, certain sounds could still trigger his trauma.
Discuss, in whatever way feels comfortable, how you think people can grow stronger after experiencing trauma.

general.title: Emergence
talkingPoints: The way complex patterns or behaviors arise from the interaction of simpler parts within a system.
The flocking behavior of birds is a classic example of emergence, with no single bird directing the pattern.
Share an example of emergence you've noticed, where a group produced something no individual member intended or planned.

general.title: Moral imagination
talkingPoints: The capacity to imagine the ethical dimensions of a situation and envision possibilities beyond the obvious choices.
Resolving the dispute required moral imagination to find a solution neither side had considered.
Describe a conflict where exercising moral imagination helped you see options you hadn't initially considered.

random.title: Under the weather
talkingPoints: Feeling slightly ill or not in your usual good health.
I stayed home from work because I was feeling under the weather.
Describe the last time you felt under the weather and how you dealt with it.

random.title: Kill two birds with one stone
talkingPoints: To achieve two goals with a single action.
By biking to work, I kill two birds with one stone: commuting and exercising.
Describe a time you killed two birds with one stone by combining two tasks.

random.title: Kick the bucket
talkingPoints: An informal, often humorous way of saying that someone has died.
My grandfather always joked that he'd travel the world before he kicked the bucket.
Talk about something on your bucket list you want to do before you kick the bucket.

random.title: Give the benefit of the doubt
talkingPoints: To believe someone's explanation or trust them without full proof, rather than assuming the worst.
She was late again, but I gave her the benefit of the doubt since traffic was bad.
Describe a time you gave someone the benefit of the doubt, and how it turned out.

random.title: A wolf in sheep's clothing
talkingPoints: Someone who appears harmless or friendly but is actually dangerous or deceptive.
The salesman seemed friendly at first, but he turned out to be a wolf in sheep's clothing.
Describe a time you realized someone was a wolf in sheep's clothing.

random.title: Pull yourself up by your bootstraps
talkingPoints: To improve your situation through your own hard work and effort, without relying on outside help.
She pulled herself up by her bootstraps, working three jobs to put herself through college.
Describe a time you had to pull yourself up by your bootstraps to overcome a hard situation.

random.title: Trust
talkingPoints: Firm belief in the reliability, truth, or ability of someone or something.
It takes years to build trust but only seconds to break it.
Describe how you rebuilt trust with someone after it was broken.

random.title: Future
talkingPoints: The time or period yet to come.
He was nervous but excited about the future after graduation.
Describe how you picture your life five years from now.

random.title: Creativity
talkingPoints: The use of imagination to produce original ideas or things.
Limited resources actually pushed her creativity further than she expected.
Talk about a time a limitation forced you to be more creative.

random.title: Play
talkingPoints: Activity engaged in for enjoyment and recreation rather than a serious purpose.
The kids lost themselves in play for hours in the backyard.
Describe a way you like to play or unwind that people might not expect.

random.title: Community
talkingPoints: A group of people living in the same area or sharing common interests.
The community came together to rebuild the playground after the fire.
Talk about a community you belong to and what it means to you.

random.title: Safety
talkingPoints: The condition of being protected from danger or harm.
He didn't feel truly safe until he heard his daughter's voice on the phone.
Describe a moment you realized how much safety, or the lack of it, mattered to you.

random.title: Accountability
talkingPoints: The obligation to accept responsibility for one's actions and their outcomes.
The manager modeled accountability by publicly owning the project's failure.
Describe a time you had to own up to a mistake instead of shifting the blame.

random.title: Opportunity
talkingPoints: A set of circumstances that makes it possible to do something.
A chance conversation at a conference turned into the opportunity of her career.
Describe an opportunity you almost let pass by and what made you take it.

random.title: Negotiation
talkingPoints: Discussion aimed at reaching an agreement.
Hours of negotiation finally landed both sides on a contract they could live with.
Talk about a negotiation, big or small, where you had to give up something to gain something else.

random.title: Bias
talkingPoints: A tendency to lean in a particular direction, often unfairly.
He didn't realize his own bias until someone pointed out he only hired people who reminded him of himself.
Describe a bias you've noticed in yourself and what you've done about it.

random.title: Acceptance
talkingPoints: The action of consenting to receive or undertake something; also, acknowledging a situation as it is.
Acceptance of his diagnosis, rather than denial, was what finally let him move forward.
Talk about something difficult you eventually reached acceptance about.

random.title: Conviction
talkingPoints: A firmly held belief or opinion; also, firmness of belief.
Her conviction that the project would work kept the team going after two failed prototypes.
Describe a conviction you hold so strongly that you'd defend it even if you were the only one.

random.title: Complacency
talkingPoints: A feeling of quiet satisfaction that leads to a lack of awareness of potential problems or the need for effort.
Years of success bred complacency, and the company was blindsided by a nimbler competitor.
Share a time when complacency cost you an opportunity, and how you've tried to guard against it since.

random.title: Legitimacy
talkingPoints: The quality of being accepted as rightful or valid, often referring to authority or power.
The new government struggled to establish legitimacy after a disputed election.
Explain what you think makes any authority, whether a government, a boss, or a rule, legitimate in your eyes.

random.title: Power
talkingPoints: The ability to influence or control the behavior of people or the course of events.
The senator's power came less from her title than from the relationships she'd built over years.
Talk about a time you held power over someone else, even briefly, and how you tried to use it responsibly.

random.title: Healing
talkingPoints: The process of recovering from physical, emotional, or psychological harm.
Healing from the loss took much longer than she expected.
Describe what healing has looked like for you after a difficult period in your life.

random.title: Feedback
talkingPoints: Information about the results of an action that is used to adjust future behavior.
The coach gave immediate feedback after every drill so players could correct their form.
Describe a piece of feedback that was hard to hear but ended up changing you for the better.

random.title: Disillusionment
talkingPoints: The feeling of disappointment that comes from discovering that something is not as good as it was believed to be.
His disillusionment with the company grew after he saw how differently leadership acted behind closed doors.
Share an experience of disillusionment, whether with a person, institution, or belief, and how it changed your outlook.

tech-terms.title: Cost an arm and a leg
talkingPoints: To be very expensive.
That designer handbag cost an arm and a leg.
Talk about something you bought that cost an arm and a leg and whether it was worth it.

tech-terms.title: See eye to eye
talkingPoints: To agree with someone or share the same opinion.
My sister and I don't always see eye to eye on politics.
Talk about someone you don't always see eye to eye with and how you handle it.

tech-terms.title: Leave no stone unturned
talkingPoints: To try every possible way of achieving something or solving a problem.
The detectives left no stone unturned in their search for the missing evidence.
Describe a time you left no stone unturned while trying to solve a problem.

tech-terms.title: Have an ace up your sleeve
talkingPoints: To have a hidden advantage or secret plan kept in reserve for the right moment.
Don't worry about the negotiation — I have an ace up my sleeve.
Talk about a time you had an ace up your sleeve when facing a challenge.

tech-terms.title: Don't rock the boat
talkingPoints: Don't do or say anything that will upset a stable situation or cause trouble.
Everyone agreed to keep quiet and not rock the boat before the merger was finalized.
Talk about a time you chose not to rock the boat, even though you wanted to speak up.

tech-terms.title: Bite the hand that feeds you
talkingPoints: To harm or betray someone who has helped or supported you.
Criticizing the company publicly while still on its payroll felt like biting the hand that feeds you.
Talk about a time you saw someone bite the hand that feeds them, or worried you might.

tech-terms.title: Peace
talkingPoints: A state of calm, quiet, and freedom from conflict or disturbance.
She finally found peace after weeks of stress at work.
Describe a place or moment where you feel completely at peace.

tech-terms.title: Success
talkingPoints: The accomplishment of an aim or purpose.
Her success didn't come overnight; it took years of setbacks first.
Share how you define success and a moment you felt you achieved it.

tech-terms.title: Inspiration
talkingPoints: Something or someone that stimulates creativity, motivation, or new ideas.
Watching her mother work two jobs was his biggest inspiration.
Describe a person or moment that has genuinely inspired you.

tech-terms.title: Rest
talkingPoints: A period of relaxation or freedom from activity, work, or stress.
After the marathon, all her body wanted was rest.
Talk about how you know when you truly need to rest, and what happens when you ignore it.

tech-terms.title: Neighbor
talkingPoints: A person who lives near or next to another.
Her elderly neighbor became like a second grandmother to her.
Describe a neighbor who left an unexpected impression on you.

tech-terms.title: Belonging
talkingPoints: The feeling of being accepted and valued as part of a group.
It took years abroad before she finally felt a sense of belonging.
Share a place or group where you finally felt like you belonged.

tech-terms.title: Responsibility
talkingPoints: A duty or obligation to deal with or take care of something.
Taking responsibility for the younger players changed how the captain led the team.
Talk about a responsibility you didn't ask for but grew into.

tech-terms.title: Obstacle
talkingPoints: A thing that blocks one's way or hinders progress.
Lack of funding was the biggest obstacle standing between them and launching the product.
Share a story about an obstacle that forced you to find a completely different path.

tech-terms.title: Compromise
talkingPoints: An agreement reached by each side making concessions.
The compromise wasn't perfect for either of them, but it kept the partnership alive.
Describe a compromise you made that you're still not sure was the right call.

tech-terms.title: Privilege
talkingPoints: A special right or advantage available only to a particular person or group.
Recognizing her own privilege changed how she approached mentoring first-generation students.
Talk about a privilege you've had that you didn't fully notice until later in life.

tech-terms.title: Rejection
talkingPoints: The dismissal or refusal of a proposal, idea, or person.
A dozen rejections came before the one acceptance letter that changed her career.
Describe a rejection that stung at the time but led somewhere better.

tech-terms.title: Surrender
talkingPoints: The act of giving up or ceasing resistance to an opposing force or accepting a situation.
Learning to accept help felt like a kind of surrender he wasn't used to.
Talk about a time surrendering to a situation, instead of fighting it, was actually the right call.

tech-terms.title: Skepticism
talkingPoints: An attitude of doubting claims until they are backed by sufficient evidence.
Her skepticism about the new supplement made her ask for proof before recommending it to patients.
Explain how you decide when healthy skepticism turns into unhelpful cynicism.

tech-terms.title: Complicity
talkingPoints: Involvement, often knowing, in a wrongful act committed by someone else.
By staying silent about the fraud, he became complicit in it.
Describe a situation where silence or inaction might have made you complicit in something you disagreed with.

tech-terms.title: Truth
talkingPoints: The quality of being in accordance with fact or reality.
The journalist risked her career to report the truth despite pressure to stay quiet.
Discuss whether you believe there's always an objective truth to be found, or whether some questions have no single true answer.

tech-terms.title: Justice
talkingPoints: The quality of being fair and giving people what they morally deserve.
The community demanded justice after the case was mishandled for years.
Discuss a case where you think the legal outcome and true justice were not the same thing.

tech-terms.title: Adaptation
talkingPoints: The process of adjusting to new conditions or changing circumstances.
The species' adaptation to the harsher climate took thousands of generations.
Talk about a major adaptation you've had to make in your life and what it taught you about your own flexibility.

tech-terms.title: Disenfranchisement
talkingPoints: The state of being deprived of a right, especially the right to vote or to participate meaningfully in society.
Historians studied how certain laws led to the disenfranchisement of entire communities.
Discuss a group you believe still faces disenfranchisement today, and what you think could change that.

football.title: Beat around the bush
talkingPoints: To avoid talking directly about something, usually because it is unpleasant.
Stop beating around the bush and tell me what really happened.
Share a time you beat around the bush instead of saying what you really meant.

football.title: On the fence
talkingPoints: Undecided or unable to choose between two options.
I'm still on the fence about whether to accept the new job offer.
Describe a decision where you've been sitting on the fence and what's holding you back.

football.title: On thin ice
talkingPoints: In a risky or precarious situation where a mistake could have serious consequences.
After missing another deadline, he knew he was on thin ice with his manager.
Share a time you felt you were on thin ice with someone, like a boss or teacher.

football.title: Jump the gun
talkingPoints: To act too soon, before the proper time.
We jumped the gun by announcing the launch before the product was ready.
Describe a time you jumped the gun and acted before you should have.

football.title: Wear your heart on your sleeve
talkingPoints: To openly show your emotions rather than hide them.
She's always worn her heart on her sleeve, so you always know how she feels.
Share whether you tend to wear your heart on your sleeve and how that's affected your relationships.

football.title: Reap what you sow
talkingPoints: You experience the consequences, good or bad, of your own past actions.
He studied hard all semester and reaped what he sowed with top grades.
Describe a time you reaped what you sowed, for better or worse.

football.title: Love
talkingPoints: A deep feeling of affection and care for someone or something.
Their love for each other grew stronger through hard times.
Talk about someone whose love shaped who you are today.

football.title: Happiness
talkingPoints: The state of feeling pleasure, contentment, or joy.
Real happiness for him meant simple mornings with his kids.
Talk about what genuinely makes you happy, beyond the obvious answers.

football.title: Motivation
talkingPoints: The reason or drive behind a person's actions or behavior.
His motivation to finish the race came from a promise to his late father.
Talk about what motivates you when you feel like giving up.

football.title: Work
talkingPoints: Activity involving mental or physical effort done to achieve a purpose, especially a job.
He found unexpected meaning in work he once considered boring.
Describe a job or task that taught you something about yourself.

football.title: Stranger
talkingPoints: A person one does not know.
A stranger's kind words on the train stayed with him for weeks.
Share a meaningful moment you had with a complete stranger.

football.title: Identity
talkingPoints: The qualities, beliefs, and characteristics that define a person or group.
Moving to a new country forced him to rethink parts of his identity.
Talk about something that has shaped your sense of identity.

football.title: Leadership
talkingPoints: The action of leading a group of people or an organization.
Her calm leadership during the crisis kept the whole department steady.
Describe a moment you had to lead even though nobody put you in charge.

football.title: Solution
talkingPoints: A means of solving a problem or dealing with a difficult situation.
The simplest solution turned out to be the one everyone had overlooked.
Talk about a problem you solved in a way nobody expected.

football.title: Boundaries
talkingPoints: Limits that define acceptable behavior or that separate one thing from another.
Setting clear boundaries at work finally gave her evenings back for herself.
Talk about a boundary you had to set with someone close to you, and how they reacted.

football.title: Inequality
talkingPoints: Difference in size, degree, or circumstances, especially an unfair difference in status or opportunity.
The report exposed the stark inequality in pay between departments doing nearly identical work.
Describe an example of inequality you've witnessed firsthand and how it affected you.

football.title: Validation
talkingPoints: Recognition or affirmation that a person or their feelings are valid or worthwhile.
He'd spent years chasing validation from people who were never going to give it.
Talk about a time you needed validation from someone and either got it or learned to live without it.

football.title: Endurance
talkingPoints: The capacity to withstand hardship or stress over a long period.
Finishing the marathon came down to endurance more than speed.
Describe a long, difficult stretch that tested your endurance more than any single moment.

football.title: Nihilism
talkingPoints: The belief that life lacks inherent meaning, purpose, or value.
His nihilism made it hard for him to feel motivated by long-term goals.
Discuss how you would respond to someone who argues that nothing really matters in the end.

football.title: Culpability
talkingPoints: The degree to which someone deserves blame for a wrongful act.
The court had to weigh the culpability of each person involved in the scheme.
Discuss how you decide the level of culpability someone deserves when they were pressured into wrongdoing by others.

football.title: Perception
talkingPoints: The way something is understood or interpreted through the senses or the mind.
Two witnesses gave different accounts because their perception of the event differed.
Describe a time your perception of a person or event turned out to be wrong, and what changed your mind.

football.title: Equity
talkingPoints: Fairness achieved by accounting for individual circumstances rather than treating everyone identically.
The scholarship program was designed around equity, giving more support to students with fewer resources.
Explain the difference between equality and equity using an example from your own life or community.

football.title: Evolution
talkingPoints: A gradual process of change and development over time.
The evolution of the company's mission reflected changes in what its customers valued most.
Trace the evolution of one of your own beliefs or habits from where it started to where it is now.

football.title: Structural inequality
talkingPoints: Systematic disadvantage built into the policies, institutions, or norms of a society, rather than caused by individual actions alone.
Researchers pointed to unequal school funding as a driver of structural inequality between neighborhoods.
Describe an example of structural inequality you've observed and explain what you think would be needed to actually fix it.

science.title: Spill the beans
talkingPoints: To reveal secret information, often accidentally or before the right time.
He accidentally spilled the beans about the surprise party.
Describe a time someone spilled the beans about a secret you were keeping.

science.title: Go the extra mile
talkingPoints: To make more effort than is expected in order to achieve or help with something.
Our teacher always goes the extra mile to help students who are struggling.
Share a time you went the extra mile for someone else, or someone did it for you.

science.title: Steal someone's thunder
talkingPoints: To take credit for someone else's achievement, or to draw attention away from them.
She announced her engagement at my graduation party and stole my thunder.
Describe a time someone stole your thunder, or you accidentally stole someone else's.

science.title: Keep your cards close to your chest
talkingPoints: To keep your plans, intentions, or feelings secret from others.
During the negotiation, she kept her cards close to her chest and revealed nothing.
Share a situation where you kept your cards close to your chest instead of sharing your plans.

science.title: Go against the grain
talkingPoints: To do something that goes against the usual or expected way of doing things.
Choosing an unconventional career path went against the grain of my family's expectations.
Describe a decision you made that went against the grain of what was expected of you.

science.title: Cast pearls before swine
talkingPoints: To offer something valuable to people who won't appreciate or understand it.
Giving that detailed advice to someone who wasn't listening felt like casting pearls before swine.
Share a time you felt like you were casting pearls before swine with advice or effort that went unappreciated.

science.title: Joy
talkingPoints: A feeling of great happiness and delight.
Watching her daughter take her first steps filled her with joy.
Describe a small everyday moment that fills you with unexpected joy.

science.title: Balance
talkingPoints: A state in which different elements are equal or in correct proportions.
Finding balance between work and family took her years to learn.
Describe a time your life felt out of balance and how you fixed it.

science.title: Discipline
talkingPoints: The practice of training oneself to follow rules or a particular code of behavior.
Waking up at 5 a.m. every day took serious discipline.
Share a habit that required real discipline to build.

science.title: Food
talkingPoints: Any nutritious substance eaten to sustain life and growth.
Her grandmother's cooking was the kind of food that felt like a hug.
Talk about a dish that instantly transports you back to a specific memory.

science.title: Animal
talkingPoints: A living organism that feeds on organic matter, typically able to move and respond to its surroundings.
The rescue animal turned out to be the calmest, most loyal dog he'd ever had.
Talk about an animal, wild or pet, that has taught you something.

science.title: Purpose
talkingPoints: A reason for which something is done or exists; a sense of meaning or direction.
Volunteering gave her a sense of purpose she hadn't felt since retiring.
Describe a moment you felt a strong sense of purpose.

science.title: Innovation
talkingPoints: The introduction of new ideas, methods, or products.
The company's culture of innovation pushed engineers to test wild ideas without fear of failure.
Talk about a creative solution you came up with when the usual approach wasn't working.

science.title: Critical thinking
talkingPoints: The objective analysis and evaluation of an issue in order to form a judgment.
Critical thinking helped her spot the flaw in the plan before it cost the company money.
Describe a time your critical thinking stopped you from making a bad decision.

science.title: Expectations
talkingPoints: Strong beliefs about how something should be or what someone should achieve.
Living up to his family's expectations weighed on him more than the job itself.
Describe a time someone's expectations of you didn't match your own, and how you handled it.

science.title: Empowerment
talkingPoints: The process of becoming stronger and more confident, especially in controlling one's own life.
The workshop's focus on empowerment gave the young women tools to negotiate their own salaries.
Talk about a moment someone or something empowered you to take control of a situation.

science.title: Recognition
talkingPoints: Acknowledgment of someone's achievements, qualities, or existence.
Public recognition for the project meant less to her than her team's quiet thank-you.
Describe a moment of recognition that meant more to you than you expected.

science.title: Patience
talkingPoints: The capacity to accept delay, trouble, or suffering without becoming annoyed.
It took real patience to teach her grandmother to use a smartphone one step at a time.
Talk about a situation that forced you to practice patience you didn't know you had.

science.title: Humanism
talkingPoints: A worldview that emphasizes human value, reason, and dignity over supernatural or divine authority.
Renaissance humanism placed human potential and achievement at the center of art and thought.
Talk about what it would mean to build your own ethics primarily around human dignity and reason rather than tradition or religion.

science.title: Subjectivity
talkingPoints: The quality of being based on personal feelings, perspective, or interpretation rather than external facts.
The reviewer admitted that much of her rating relied on subjectivity rather than objective standards.
Explain an area of your life, like taste in art or humor, where you fully embrace subjectivity rather than seeking one right answer.

science.title: Reality
talkingPoints: The state of things as they actually exist, independent of ideas or beliefs about them.
No matter how much he wished otherwise, reality eventually forced him to accept the diagnosis.
Discuss a moment when your idea of reality collided with the actual facts, and how you adjusted.

science.title: Fairness
talkingPoints: The quality of making judgments or treating people free from favoritism or discrimination.
The referee was praised for his fairness even when the calls went against the home team.
Describe a situation where something was technically by the rules but still felt unfair to you, and explain why.

science.title: Revolution
talkingPoints: A sudden, radical, or complete change, especially in a political system or set of ideas.
The digital revolution transformed how people communicate and access information.
Discuss whether you think a certain broken system in your life or society needs gradual reform or an outright revolution.

science.title: Cultural capital
talkingPoints: The knowledge, habits, tastes, and credentials that give a person social advantage within a particular society.
Knowing which fork to use at a formal dinner was a small but telling form of cultural capital.
Discuss a form of cultural capital you grew up with or without, and how it shaped the opportunities available to you.

history.title: Once in a blue moon
talkingPoints: Very rarely; almost never.
We only go to the movies once in a blue moon these days.
Talk about something you only get to do once in a blue moon and why.

history.title: Let the cat out of the bag
talkingPoints: To reveal a secret, usually without meaning to.
My little brother let the cat out of the bag about my birthday surprise.
Describe a time you let the cat out of the bag about something you weren't supposed to share.

history.title: The last straw
talkingPoints: The final small problem in a series that makes a situation unbearable.
The third missed deadline was the last straw, and the client ended the contract.
Talk about a moment that was the last straw in a difficult relationship or situation.

history.title: Kick the can down the road
talkingPoints: To postpone dealing with a problem instead of resolving it now.
The committee kept kicking the can down the road instead of fixing the budget issue.
Describe a problem in your life you've been kicking the can down the road on.

history.title: Strike while the iron is hot
talkingPoints: To take advantage of an opportunity as soon as it appears.
Sales were up, so we struck while the iron was hot and launched the new product line early.
Talk about a time you struck while the iron was hot and seized an opportunity quickly.

history.title: The road to hell is paved with good intentions
talkingPoints: Good intentions alone are not enough; they can still lead to bad outcomes if not followed through properly.
He meant to help by reorganizing the files, but he broke the system — the road to hell is paved with good intentions.
Describe a time your good intentions led to an unexpected bad outcome.

history.title: Strength
talkingPoints: Physical power, or the mental and emotional resilience to endure hardship.
He drew on inner strength to get through the loss of his job.
Share a time you discovered a strength in yourself you didn't know you had.

history.title: Change
talkingPoints: The act or process of becoming different.
Moving to a new city forced him to embrace change.
Talk about a change you resisted at first but later welcomed.

history.title: Focus
talkingPoints: The center of attention or concentrated effort on a single task.
She struggled to keep her focus during the long study session.
Describe a time you had to fight hard to stay focused.

history.title: Music
talkingPoints: Vocal or instrumental sounds combined to produce beauty of form, harmony, and emotion.
Music got him through some of the hardest nights of that year.
Share a song that means something deeply personal to you, and why.

history.title: Garden
talkingPoints: A piece of ground used for growing plants, flowers, or vegetables.
Tending the garden every morning became her form of meditation.
Describe a garden, or any space, where you go to clear your head.

history.title: Simplicity
talkingPoints: The quality of being easy to understand or uncomplicated.
After years of chasing more, he found real peace in simplicity.
Talk about a time simplifying something in your life made it better.

history.title: Curiosity
talkingPoints: A strong desire to know or learn something.
Her curiosity about how things worked eventually led her into engineering.
Share a question you couldn't stop chasing and where it eventually led you.

history.title: Decision-making
talkingPoints: The process of making choices by identifying options and weighing their outcomes.
Fast decision-making under pressure is what separated the two candidates in the interview.
Talk about a tough decision you had to make with incomplete information.

history.title: Standards
talkingPoints: Levels of quality or achievement that are considered acceptable or desirable.
The chef refused to lower his standards even when the restaurant was losing money.
Talk about a standard you hold yourself to that most people around you don't.

history.title: Autonomy
talkingPoints: The right or condition of self-governance; independence.
Being given full autonomy over the project was terrifying at first, then liberating.
Describe a time you were given real autonomy and what you did with it.

history.title: Reputation
talkingPoints: The beliefs or opinions that are generally held about someone or something.
It took years to build his reputation as reliable, and one missed deadline to shake it.
Talk about how your reputation, at work or elsewhere, was built and what it cost to maintain.

history.title: Humility
talkingPoints: A modest or low view of one's own importance.
Despite the award, his humility meant he spent the speech thanking everyone but himself.
Describe a moment that taught you humility, especially after a success.

history.title: Determinism
talkingPoints: The idea that all events, including human choices, are ultimately caused by prior events and could not have happened otherwise.
If determinism is true, some argue, then true moral responsibility becomes difficult to justify.
Argue whether you believe your choices are truly free or simply the product of your genes and environment.

history.title: Objectivity
talkingPoints: The quality of being based on observable facts rather than personal feelings or bias.
Journalists strive for objectivity even when covering emotionally charged events.
Discuss whether you believe true objectivity is actually possible, or whether every viewpoint carries some bias.

history.title: Illusion
talkingPoints: A false idea or belief, or something that appears different from what it actually is.
The magician's trick relied on a simple optical illusion.
Share an illusion you once believed about yourself or the world, and what shattered it.

history.title: Dignity
talkingPoints: The state of being worthy of respect, regardless of circumstances.
Even in poverty, the family insisted on being treated with dignity.
Talk about a time you saw someone maintain their dignity in a difficult or humiliating situation.

history.title: Sustainability
talkingPoints: The ability to maintain a process or system over the long term without depleting the resources it depends on.
The farm switched to crop rotation to improve the sustainability of its soil.
Talk about one habit in your own life, like your work pace or spending, that you suspect isn't truly sustainable long term.

history.title: Social mobility
talkingPoints: The ability of individuals or families to move between different social or economic levels over time.
Economists study education access as one of the strongest predictors of social mobility.
Talk about a factor that has helped or hindered social mobility in your own family's story.

tech.title: Back to square one
talkingPoints: Back to the very beginning, usually after a failed attempt.
The deal fell through, so we're back to square one on finding investors.
Describe a project or plan that sent you back to square one.

tech.title: Bite off more than you can chew
talkingPoints: To take on more responsibility or work than you are able to handle.
Volunteering for three committees at once, I really bit off more than I could chew.
Talk about a time you bit off more than you could chew and how you managed it.

tech.title: Cut corners
talkingPoints: To do something in the easiest or cheapest way, often sacrificing quality.
The contractor cut corners on materials, and the roof leaked within a year.
Share a time you cut corners on a task and whether it came back to bite you.

tech.title: Leave someone in the lurch
talkingPoints: To abandon someone in a difficult situation without help or warning.
My business partner left me in the lurch right before our biggest client meeting.
Talk about a time someone left you in the lurch, or you had to leave someone else that way.

tech.title: Rest on your laurels
talkingPoints: To become so satisfied with past success that you stop trying to achieve more.
After winning the award, he rested on his laurels and stopped improving his craft.
Describe a time you rested on your laurels after a success, and what happened next.

tech.title: Let the chips fall where they may
talkingPoints: To let events happen naturally without trying to control the outcome.
I've done all I can for the presentation; now I'll let the chips fall where they may.
Talk about a time you decided to let the chips fall where they may instead of trying to control everything.

tech.title: Wisdom
talkingPoints: The quality of having experience, knowledge, and good judgment.
Her grandmother's wisdom helped her make the right decision.
Talk about a piece of wisdom someone gave you that you still think about.

tech.title: Growth
talkingPoints: The process of developing or maturing physically, mentally, or emotionally.
Every failure was part of her personal growth, she realized later.
Share a hard experience that led to real growth for you.

tech.title: Action
talkingPoints: The process of doing something to achieve a goal.
Talk was cheap; it was his action that finally convinced them.
Talk about a time you chose to take action instead of just talking about it.

tech.title: Color
talkingPoints: The property of an object that produces different sensations of light on the eye.
The color of the sky that evening was something she'd never forget.
Describe a color that carries a strong memory or emotion for you.

tech.title: Story
talkingPoints: An account of imaginary or real events told for entertainment or information.
Her grandfather's war story was one she never got tired of hearing.
Share a story that gets told over and over in your family.

tech.title: Curiosity
talkingPoints: A strong desire to know or learn something.
Her curiosity about the abandoned house led her to knock on the door.
Share something your curiosity led you to discover or try.

tech.title: Ambition
talkingPoints: A strong desire to achieve something, typically requiring determination and hard work.
His ambition to open his own restaurant kept him working double shifts for years.
Describe an ambition you're chasing right now and what you're willing to sacrifice for it.

tech.title: Risk-taking
talkingPoints: The act of engaging in actions that involve danger or uncertainty in pursuit of a goal.
Her willingness for risk-taking led her to quit a stable job and start her own business.
Share a risk you took that didn't pay off immediately but taught you something valuable.

tech.title: Values
talkingPoints: Principles or standards of behavior that a person judges to be important in life.
Their shared values, more than shared interests, were what made the friendship last.
Describe a value you hold that has actually cost you something to live by.

tech.title: Dependency
talkingPoints: The state of relying on someone or something else for support.
His dependency on constant approval from his boss made every review nerve-wracking.
Talk about a dependency, on a person, habit, or thing, you've had to work to loosen.

tech.title: Perception
talkingPoints: The way in which something is regarded, understood, or interpreted.
Public perception of the company shifted overnight after the apology video went viral.
Describe a time your perception of a person or situation turned out to be completely wrong.

tech.title: Arrogance
talkingPoints: An exaggerated sense of one's own importance or abilities.
His arrogance in the negotiation nearly cost the company the deal.
Talk about a time arrogance, yours or someone else's, got in the way of something important.

tech.title: Free will
talkingPoints: The capacity to make choices that are not fully determined by prior causes.
Debates about free will ask whether we could have chosen differently in a given moment.
Describe a decision you made and argue whether you truly could have chosen otherwise or whether it was inevitable given who you are.

tech.title: Ambiguity
talkingPoints: The quality of having more than one possible meaning or interpretation, creating uncertainty.
The contract's ambiguity led both sides to interpret the clause differently.
Share how comfortable you are living with ambiguity when a situation doesn't have a clear right answer.

tech.title: Certainty
talkingPoints: The state of being completely confident that something is true.
She spoke with such certainty that no one in the room dared to question her.
Discuss whether you think certainty is a virtue or a trap when it comes to your own beliefs.

tech.title: Rights
talkingPoints: Entitlements or freedoms that are morally or legally guaranteed to a person.
The protesters marched to demand equal rights under the law.
Discuss which right you would fight hardest to protect if it were ever threatened, and why.

tech.title: Scarcity
talkingPoints: A shortage or insufficient supply of something needed or desired.
Water scarcity forced the region to ration its supply during the drought.
Describe how a mindset of scarcity versus abundance has shaped a major decision you've made.

tech.title: Invisible labor
talkingPoints: Work that is essential but goes unrecognized, uncompensated, or unnoticed, often domestic or emotional in nature.
The invisible labor of managing the household schedule fell almost entirely on one parent.
Describe a form of invisible labor you or someone close to you performs that rarely gets acknowledged.

finance.title: The ball is in your court
talkingPoints: It is now your responsibility to take the next action or make a decision.
I've given you all the information, so the ball is in your court now.
Talk about a moment when the ball was in your court and how you responded.

finance.title: Miss the boat
talkingPoints: To lose an opportunity by acting too slowly.
By the time I applied, the positions were filled — I missed the boat.
Describe an opportunity you feel you missed the boat on.

finance.title: Speak of the devil
talkingPoints: Said when a person who was just being talked about suddenly appears.
Speak of the devil — we were just talking about you!
Describe a funny coincidence when someone showed up right as you were talking about them.

finance.title: Let sleeping dogs lie
talkingPoints: To avoid interfering with a situation that could cause trouble if disturbed.
The issue was resolved years ago, so it's best to let sleeping dogs lie.
Describe a past conflict you decided to let sleeping dogs lie on rather than reopen.

finance.title: A flash in the pan
talkingPoints: Something that appears impressive briefly but does not last or lead to lasting success.
The band's first hit turned out to be a flash in the pan; they never released another popular song.
Talk about a success in your life that turned out to be a flash in the pan.

finance.title: A stitch in time saves nine
talkingPoints: Dealing with a small problem right away can prevent it from becoming a much bigger one later.
Fixing the small leak now is a stitch in time that will save nine repairs later.
Share a time a stitch in time saved you from a bigger problem, or a time you wish it had.

finance.title: Honesty
talkingPoints: The quality of being truthful and sincere.
His honesty about the mistake earned his boss's respect.
Describe a time being honest was hard but ultimately the right choice.

finance.title: Learning
talkingPoints: The acquisition of knowledge or skills through study or experience.
Learning a new language as an adult humbled him.
Describe something difficult you've learned recently and how you learned it.

finance.title: Practice
talkingPoints: Repeated exercise in an activity to improve or maintain a skill.
Years of daily practice finally paid off at the recital.
Describe something you got better at only because you kept practicing.

finance.title: Light
talkingPoints: The natural agent that makes things visible; also a symbol of hope or guidance.
The first light of morning always gave him a strange sense of hope.
Talk about a moment someone or something was a 'light' during a dark time.

finance.title: Song
talkingPoints: A short piece of music with lyrics, meant to be sung.
That one song could instantly bring her back to her college dorm room.
Talk about a song that changes your mood the instant it starts playing.

finance.title: Passion
talkingPoints: A strong and barely controllable emotion or enthusiasm for something.
His passion for cooking eventually turned into a small restaurant of his own.
Talk about a passion of yours and how it started.

finance.title: Determination
talkingPoints: Firmness of purpose; resoluteness.
Sheer determination got her across the finish line after she twisted her ankle.
Talk about a time your determination outlasted your motivation.

finance.title: Vision
talkingPoints: An idea or image of what the future could or should be like.
The founder's vision for the company kept the team focused even during the hardest years.
Describe the vision you have for your own future five years from now.

finance.title: Principles
talkingPoints: Fundamental truths or propositions that serve as a foundation for behavior.
He built the entire company on the principle that customers come before profit.
Talk about a principle you refused to bend on, even under pressure.

finance.title: Sacrifice
talkingPoints: The act of giving up something valued for the sake of something else considered more important.
Her parents' sacrifice of a comfortable life abroad gave her a shot at a better education.
Describe a sacrifice someone made for you, or one you made for someone else.

finance.title: Narrative
talkingPoints: A spoken or written account of connected events; a particular way of presenting a situation.
Changing the narrative around the failed launch helped the team see it as a lesson, not a disaster.
Talk about the narrative you tell yourself about a hard chapter in your life.

finance.title: Envy
talkingPoints: A feeling of discontented longing for someone else's advantages or possessions.
Envy crept in every time she scrolled past a friend's vacation photos.
Describe a moment of envy that taught you something about what you actually want.

finance.title: Dualism
talkingPoints: The view that reality consists of two fundamentally different kinds of substance, most often mind and body.
Descartes' dualism separated the thinking mind from the physical body.
Explain whether you think your mind is something separate from your brain, or simply what your brain does.

finance.title: Nuance
talkingPoints: A subtle distinction or shade of meaning, attitude, or feeling.
Her essay captured the nuance of the debate instead of reducing it to two simple sides.
Talk about a topic where you feel most people miss the nuance and oversimplify into two extreme positions.

finance.title: Doubt
talkingPoints: A feeling of uncertainty about the truth or reliability of something.
Doubt crept in the night before the exam, even though she'd studied for weeks.
Describe a time doubt actually helped you make a better decision instead of holding you back.

finance.title: Obligation
talkingPoints: A duty or commitment to do something, often because of a moral or legal requirement.
He felt a strong obligation to repay the kindness his mentor had shown him.
Describe an obligation you carry that no one would blame you for walking away from, and explain why you don't.

finance.title: Abundance
talkingPoints: A very large quantity of something, more than enough to meet a need.
The harvest that year brought an abundance of vegetables the family couldn't use fast enough.
Discuss an area of your life where you feel genuine abundance, and how that differs from areas where you feel scarcity.

finance.title: Privilege
talkingPoints: An unearned advantage or benefit granted to certain people because of their social position, identity, or circumstances.
Growing up with stable housing was a form of privilege he hadn't recognized until he saw others struggle without it.
Reflect on a privilege you've benefited from without choosing it, and how awareness of it has, or hasn't, changed your actions.

roast.title: Call it a day
talkingPoints: To decide to stop working on something, usually for the rest of the day.
We've made great progress, so let's call it a day and finish tomorrow.
Describe a time you had to call it a day even though the work wasn't finished.

roast.title: Jump on the bandwagon
talkingPoints: To join others in doing something that has become popular or fashionable.
Once the diet became trendy, everyone at the office jumped on the bandwagon.
Share a trend you jumped on the bandwagon for, and whether you regret it.

roast.title: Turn a blind eye
talkingPoints: To deliberately ignore something you know is wrong.
The manager turned a blind eye to the employees arriving late every day.
Talk about a time you turned a blind eye to something, or someone did it for you.

roast.title: Look a gift horse in the mouth
talkingPoints: To criticize or question something that has been given to you for free.
The car has a few scratches, but it was free, so don't look a gift horse in the mouth.
Share a time you almost looked a gift horse in the mouth instead of just being grateful.

roast.title: Gild the lily
talkingPoints: To add unnecessary decoration or embellishment to something that is already good enough.
The dessert was perfect on its own, so adding three sauces was just gilding the lily.
Describe a time you gilded the lily by over-improving something that was already fine.

roast.title: The proof is in the pudding
talkingPoints: The real value or quality of something can only be judged by putting it into practice or trying it.
The new strategy sounds great on paper, but the proof is in the pudding.
Describe a plan or idea where the proof was really in the pudding once you tried it.

roast.title: Respect
talkingPoints: Admiration for someone based on their abilities, qualities, or achievements.
The young coach quickly earned the respect of his players.
Talk about someone you respect deeply and explain why.

roast.title: Teaching
talkingPoints: The act of helping someone acquire knowledge or skill.
Teaching her younger brother to read was one of her proudest moments.
Talk about a time you taught someone something and what you learned from it.

roast.title: Smile
talkingPoints: A pleased, kind, or amused facial expression formed by curving the mouth upward.
A stranger's smile on a rough day made her feel a little lighter.
Talk about a smile that stuck with you, from a stranger or someone close.

roast.title: Shadow
talkingPoints: A dark area created when an object blocks light; also something that lingers unseen.
The shadow of his father's disapproval followed him into adulthood.
Describe something from your past that still casts a shadow over you today.

roast.title: Letter
talkingPoints: A written or printed message addressed to a person or organization.
The old letter from his grandmother was worn soft from being read so often.
Describe a letter, written or received, that meant something to you.

roast.title: Warmth
talkingPoints: The quality of being warm in temperature, or friendly and affectionate in manner.
The warmth in her voice made even strangers feel instantly at ease.
Describe someone whose warmth left a lasting impression on you.

roast.title: Confidence
talkingPoints: The feeling of self-assurance arising from an appreciation of one's own abilities.
Years of practice gave her the confidence to walk on stage without notes.
Describe a moment you had to fake confidence before you actually felt it.

roast.title: Mission
talkingPoints: An important assignment or purpose that a person or group is committed to.
The nonprofit's mission to house every family in the county shaped every decision they made.
Talk about a personal mission that guides how you spend your time.

roast.title: Ethics
talkingPoints: Moral principles that govern a person's behavior or the conducting of an activity.
The board debated the ethics of using customer data without explicit consent.
Describe a situation where you had to think hard about the ethics of a decision.

roast.title: Loyalty
talkingPoints: A strong feeling of support or allegiance.
Her loyalty to the small team kept her from taking a higher-paying offer elsewhere.
Talk about a time your loyalty to someone or something was truly tested.

roast.title: Stereotype
talkingPoints: A widely held but oversimplified image or idea of a particular type of person or thing.
Working alongside her broke every stereotype he'd unconsciously carried about her profession.
Describe a stereotype you once believed and the experience that changed your mind.

roast.title: Jealousy
talkingPoints: A feeling of resentment against someone because of their success, advantage, or relationships.
Jealousy over his brother's promotion strained their relationship for months.
Talk about a time jealousy showed up in a relationship and how you dealt with it.

roast.title: Moral relativism
talkingPoints: The view that moral judgments are true or false only relative to a particular culture or individual, not universally.
Moral relativism would say that a practice can be right in one culture and wrong in another.
Take a stand on whether some moral truths, like the wrongness of cruelty, hold across every culture regardless of local belief.

roast.title: Context
talkingPoints: The circumstances or background that give meaning to an event, statement, or idea.
Without context, the quote sounded much harsher than the speaker had intended.
Describe a time when missing context caused you to misjudge a person or situation.

roast.title: Belief
talkingPoints: An acceptance that something is true, even without complete proof.
His belief in the project kept the team going through months of setbacks.
Talk about a belief you've held for a long time and explain what evidence, if any, would change your mind.

roast.title: Duty
talkingPoints: A moral or legal responsibility to act in a certain way.
She saw caring for her aging parents as a duty, not a burden.
Talk about a duty in your life that sometimes conflicts with your personal desires, and how you navigate that tension.

roast.title: Trade-off
talkingPoints: A balancing of two desirable but conflicting outcomes, where gaining one means giving up some of the other.
Choosing a smaller apartment closer to work was a trade-off she was willing to make for a shorter commute.
Describe a major trade-off you've made in your life and explain whether, looking back, you'd choose the same way again.

pitch.title: Don't judge a book by its cover
talkingPoints: You shouldn't judge someone or something based only on outward appearance.
He seemed unfriendly at first, but don't judge a book by its cover — he's actually very kind.
Share a time you learned not to judge a book by its cover after misjudging someone.

pitch.title: Pull someone's leg
talkingPoints: To joke with someone by telling them something untrue in a playful way.
Relax, I was just pulling your leg — the meeting isn't cancelled.
Describe a time a friend or family member was pulling your leg and you didn't realize it at first.

pitch.title: Hit the ground running
talkingPoints: To start a new activity or job with energy and enthusiasm right from the beginning.
She hit the ground running on her first day, closing two deals by lunch.
Describe a time you hit the ground running in a new job, school, or project.

pitch.title: Move the goalposts
talkingPoints: To unfairly change the rules or requirements of a situation partway through.
First they wanted five years of experience, then they moved the goalposts to ten.
Describe a time someone moved the goalposts on you after you'd already met the original expectations.

pitch.title: Between the devil and the deep blue sea
talkingPoints: Forced to choose between two equally unpleasant or dangerous options.
Staying in a bad job or quitting with no savings left her between the devil and the deep blue sea.
Share a time you felt stuck between the devil and the deep blue sea.

pitch.title: Cross the Rubicon
talkingPoints: To take a decisive, irreversible step that commits you to a course of action.
Signing the resignation letter meant she had crossed the Rubicon; there was no going back.
Talk about a decision you made that felt like crossing the Rubicon, with no turning back.

pitch.title: Freedom
talkingPoints: The power or right to act, speak, or think without restraint.
Traveling alone gave her a sense of freedom she'd never felt before.
Describe a moment when you truly felt free.

pitch.title: Helping
talkingPoints: The act of assisting or supporting someone.
Helping his neighbor move furniture turned into a lasting friendship.
Describe a time helping someone else ended up helping you too.

pitch.title: Laughter
talkingPoints: The action of laughing, often in response to something funny.
Their laughter echoed through the house long after the joke was over.
Share a memory that still makes you laugh every time you think of it.

pitch.title: Rain
talkingPoints: Water falling in drops from clouds.
They danced in the rain like nobody was watching.
Share a memory tied to rain, good or bad.

pitch.title: Morning
talkingPoints: The early part of the day, from sunrise until noon.
Her morning routine was the one thing she never let anyone interrupt.
Talk about your ideal morning and why it matters to you.

pitch.title: Clarity
talkingPoints: The quality of being clear, easy to understand, or free of confusion.
It took a long walk alone before she found the clarity she needed.
Share a moment you suddenly gained clarity about a difficult decision.

pitch.title: Self-awareness
talkingPoints: Conscious knowledge of one's own character, feelings, motives, and desires.
A hard conversation with a mentor gave him the self-awareness to see his blind spots.
Share something about yourself you only realized after someone else pointed it out.

pitch.title: Purpose
talkingPoints: A sense of meaning or reason for existing or doing something.
Volunteering at the shelter gave her a sense of purpose she hadn't felt in years.
Describe a moment you felt a strong sense of purpose in what you were doing.

pitch.title: Morality
talkingPoints: Principles concerning the distinction between right and wrong behavior.
The film raised uncomfortable questions about the morality of wartime decisions.
Talk about a moment your sense of morality was tested by a real situation, not a hypothetical one.

pitch.title: Betrayal
talkingPoints: The act of being disloyal or breaking someone's trust.
The betrayal by his closest business partner took years to get over.
Describe a betrayal, big or small, and what it taught you about trust.

pitch.title: Expectation
talkingPoints: A strong belief that something will happen or that someone should act a certain way.
Her own expectation of perfection was harder on her than any critic ever was.
Talk about an expectation you set for yourself that you eventually had to let go of.

pitch.title: Forgiveness
talkingPoints: The action of ceasing to feel resentment against someone for an offense.
Forgiveness came slowly, years after the argument that split the family apart.
Describe a moment of forgiveness, giving it or receiving it, that changed a relationship.

pitch.title: Social contract
talkingPoints: The implicit agreement among members of a society to cooperate for mutual benefit, often by accepting certain rules and authority.
Philosophers describe paying taxes as part of the social contract citizens accept in exchange for protection and services.
Discuss what you think citizens owe their government, and what a government must do to keep its side of the social contract.

pitch.title: Agency
talkingPoints: The capacity of an individual to act independently and make their own choices.
The program was designed to give young people more agency over their own education.
Reflect on an area of your life where you feel you have real agency, and one where you feel constrained.

pitch.title: Meaning
talkingPoints: The significance, purpose, or value that something holds for a person.
She found new meaning in her work after volunteering at the shelter.
Explain where you currently find the most meaning in your life, and whether that has changed over time.

pitch.title: Virtue
talkingPoints: A positive character trait considered morally good, such as honesty or courage.
Patience was the virtue he had to work hardest to develop.
Identify the virtue you admire most in others but find hardest to practice yourself, and explain why.

pitch.title: Opportunity cost
talkingPoints: The value of the next best alternative that is given up when a choice is made.
The opportunity cost of going to graduate school was the salary he could have earned working full-time.
Talk about a decision where the opportunity cost was harder to accept than the decision itself.

conspiracy.title: Every cloud has a silver lining
talkingPoints: Even difficult or unpleasant situations have some positive aspect.
Losing that job was hard, but every cloud has a silver lining — it led me to a better career.
Describe a hard time in your life where every cloud had a silver lining.

conspiracy.title: Take it with a grain of salt
talkingPoints: To not fully believe something and treat it with some skepticism.
He exaggerates a lot, so take his stories with a grain of salt.
Talk about advice or news you had to take with a grain of salt.

conspiracy.title: Throw in the towel
talkingPoints: To give up or admit defeat.
After three failed attempts, he finally threw in the towel and asked for help.
Share a moment when you almost threw in the towel but kept going, or when you actually gave up.

conspiracy.title: Paint yourself into a corner
talkingPoints: To get yourself into a difficult situation with no easy way out, usually through your own choices.
By promising the client an impossible deadline, he painted himself into a corner.
Talk about a time you painted yourself into a corner and how you found a way out.

conspiracy.title: Throw the baby out with the bathwater
talkingPoints: To get rid of something valuable while trying to eliminate something unwanted.
Cancelling the whole program because of one flaw would be throwing the baby out with the bathwater.
Describe a time you nearly threw the baby out with the bathwater by overreacting to a problem.

conspiracy.title: Achilles' heel
talkingPoints: A person's weak point or vulnerability, despite their overall strength.
His pride was his Achilles' heel, often leading him to ignore good advice.
Describe your own Achilles' heel and how it has affected you.

conspiracy.title: Justice
talkingPoints: Fair treatment and behavior according to what is morally right.
The community rallied together to demand justice for the victim.
Share your thoughts on a time you saw justice served, or denied.

conspiracy.title: Giving
talkingPoints: The act of providing or donating something to others.
Giving away his old bike to a kid down the street felt better than keeping it.
Share a time giving something away taught you more than keeping it would have.

conspiracy.title: Wonder
talkingPoints: A feeling of amazement or curiosity caused by something beautiful or unfamiliar.
The child stared up at the stars in complete wonder.
Describe the last time something filled you with a real sense of wonder.

conspiracy.title: Sun
talkingPoints: The star at the center of the solar system that provides light and warmth to Earth.
The first sun of spring made the whole neighborhood come outside.
Talk about how the sun, or its absence, affects your mood.

conspiracy.title: Evening
talkingPoints: The period of time at the end of the day, before nightfall.
Their best conversations always happened on the porch in the evening.
Describe an evening that turned out more meaningful than you expected.

conspiracy.title: Energy
talkingPoints: The strength or vitality required for sustained physical or mental activity.
His energy in the room could lift everyone's mood in seconds.
Talk about what usually gives you energy when you're feeling drained.

conspiracy.title: Mindfulness
talkingPoints: The quality of being fully present and engaged in the current moment.
A daily mindfulness practice helped her stay calm under constant deadlines.
Talk about a moment when slowing down and paying attention changed how you handled something.

conspiracy.title: Legacy
talkingPoints: The lasting impact or things handed down by a person or generation.
His grandfather's legacy of generosity shaped how he treated every employee.
Talk about the legacy you'd like to leave behind, and why it matters to you.

conspiracy.title: Philosophy
talkingPoints: A theory or attitude that guides one's behavior; also the study of fundamental questions about existence.
Her personal philosophy of showing up early became the backbone of her career.
Describe a personal philosophy you live by and how you arrived at it.

conspiracy.title: Redemption
talkingPoints: The act of making up for a past mistake or wrongdoing.
His redemption came years later, when the same community he'd let down welcomed him back.
Talk about a moment of redemption in your life, where you made up for something you regretted.

conspiracy.title: Pressure
talkingPoints: The use of persuasion or intimidation to make someone do something; a feeling of stress.
The pressure to perform in front of investors nearly made him forget his own pitch.
Describe a high-pressure moment and how you managed to stay steady through it.

conspiracy.title: Existentialism
talkingPoints: A philosophical approach emphasizing individual existence, freedom, and choice.
Existentialism argues that we create meaning through our own choices, not through any predetermined purpose.
Explain, in your own words, whether you think life has inherent meaning or whether we create it ourselves.

conspiracy.title: Cognitive dissonance
talkingPoints: The mental discomfort felt when holding two contradictory beliefs or when actions conflict with beliefs.
He felt cognitive dissonance after preaching honesty while telling a small lie to avoid conflict.
Describe a time you experienced cognitive dissonance between what you believed and how you acted, and how you resolved it.

conspiracy.title: Autonomy
talkingPoints: The right or capacity to govern oneself and make independent decisions.
Teenagers often push for greater autonomy as they seek to make their own choices.
Discuss how you balance your own autonomy with your responsibilities to the people who depend on you.

conspiracy.title: Interpretation
talkingPoints: The act of explaining or understanding the significance of something in a particular way.
Different critics offered wildly different interpretations of the film's ending.
Share a piece of art, text, or event whose interpretation you strongly disagree with, and defend your own reading.

conspiracy.title: Character
talkingPoints: The combination of qualities that form an individual's moral and mental nature.
Losing the championship revealed more about the team's character than winning ever could.
