Describe a moment that tested your character and explain what it revealed about who you really are.

conspiracy.title: Collective action
talkingPoints: Coordinated effort by a group of people working together toward a shared goal.
It took collective action from an entire neighborhood to get the intersection made safer.
Describe a time you saw collective action succeed where individual effort alone would have failed.

worst-take.title: Hit the sack
talkingPoints: To go to bed or go to sleep.
I'm exhausted, so I'm going to hit the sack early tonight.
Talk about your usual routine before you hit the sack each night.

worst-take.title: Get out of hand
talkingPoints: To become difficult to control.
The party got out of hand once more people showed up uninvited.
Describe a situation that got out of hand and how you brought it back under control.

worst-take.title: Barking up the wrong tree
talkingPoints: Pursuing a mistaken course of action based on a wrong assumption.
If you think I ate your lunch, you're barking up the wrong tree.
Describe a time you were barking up the wrong tree while trying to solve a problem.

worst-take.title: Pass the buck
talkingPoints: To shift blame or responsibility onto someone else.
Instead of fixing the error, he passed the buck to the intern.
Describe a time someone passed the buck to you, or you passed it to someone else.

worst-take.title: Cut your coat according to your cloth
talkingPoints: To live or manage within the limits of what you actually have, especially financially.
After losing his job, he learned to cut his coat according to his cloth and cut unnecessary spending.
Talk about a time you had to cut your coat according to your cloth and live within your means.

worst-take.title: Hobson's choice
talkingPoints: A situation where you appear to have a choice but actually have only one real option.
With every other store closed, buying from the last shop was a Hobson's choice.
Share a time you faced a Hobson's choice, where you technically had options but really only one.

worst-take.title: Truth
talkingPoints: That which is factually correct or in accordance with reality.
He finally told her the truth after months of hiding it.
Talk about a time telling the truth cost you something, but was worth it.

worst-take.title: Sharing
talkingPoints: The act of dividing something and giving part of it to others.
Sharing a meal with strangers on the trip became the highlight of his journey.
Talk about a time sharing something, big or small, brought people closer.

worst-take.title: Silence
talkingPoints: The complete absence of sound; a state of quiet or stillness.
The silence after the storm felt almost louder than the storm itself.
Talk about a time silence said more than words could have.

worst-take.title: Wind
talkingPoints: The perceptible natural movement of air.
A strong wind knocked the tent over on their first camping trip.
Describe a moment being outside in the wind made you feel especially alive.

worst-take.title: Weekend
talkingPoints: The period from Friday evening or Saturday to Sunday, especially as a time of rest.
He spent every weekend that summer teaching himself to cook.
Share how you typically spend your weekends and whether that's changed over the years.

worst-take.title: Voice
talkingPoints: The sound produced through a person's mouth, or a person's right to express opinions.
Learning to use her voice in meetings took years of practice.
Describe a time you found the courage to use your voice when it mattered.

worst-take.title: Reflection
talkingPoints: Serious thought or consideration, often about past experiences.
A weekend of quiet reflection helped him decide it was time to change careers.
Describe what stepping back and reflecting on a big decision taught you.

worst-take.title: Impact
talkingPoints: A marked effect or influence.
The teacher's impact on her students lasted long after they left her classroom.
Describe a moment you realized the impact you'd had on someone else's life.

worst-take.title: Psychology
talkingPoints: The scientific study of the human mind and its functions, especially behavior.
Understanding basic psychology helped her defuse arguments before they escalated.
Talk about something you've learned about your own psychology through experience rather than a book.

worst-take.title: Reinvention
talkingPoints: The process of changing something, especially oneself, into a new form or role.
Her reinvention from accountant to potter started with one pottery class taken on a whim.
Describe a reinvention of yourself you've gone through, and what pushed you to start.

worst-take.title: Burnout
talkingPoints: A state of physical or emotional exhaustion caused by prolonged stress.
Burnout crept up on her slowly until she couldn't get through a single meeting without dreading it.
Talk about a time you recognized burnout in yourself and what you did about it.

worst-take.title: Accountability
talkingPoints: The obligation to take responsibility for one's actions and their consequences.
The manager held herself accountable for the project's failure instead of blaming her team.
Describe a moment when holding yourself accountable was harder than making an excuse would have been, and what you learned from it.

worst-take.title: Transcendence
talkingPoints: The state of rising above or going beyond ordinary physical or worldly limits.
She described the concert as a moment of transcendence that lifted her out of everyday worries.
Share an experience that felt like transcendence to you, and try to explain what made it feel that way.

worst-take.title: Alienation
talkingPoints: A feeling of isolation or estrangement from other people, society, or one's own work.
Factory workers on the assembly line sometimes described a deep alienation from the products they made.
Share a time you felt alienation, whether at work, school, or in a relationship, and what eventually helped you reconnect.

worst-take.title: Representation
talkingPoints: The depiction or portrayal of someone or something in a particular way, especially in media or politics.
The show was praised for its authentic representation of immigrant families.
Discuss why representation, whether in media, government, or the workplace, matters to you personally.

worst-take.title: Integrity
talkingPoints: The quality of being honest and having strong, consistent moral principles.
She kept her integrity by refusing to falsify the report, even under pressure from her boss.
Share a time when maintaining your integrity cost you something real, and whether you'd make the same choice again.

worst-take.title: Incentive
talkingPoints: Something that motivates or encourages a person to act in a particular way.
The company offered a bonus as an incentive for hitting the sales target early.
Discuss an incentive in your own life, financial or otherwise, that you suspect is quietly steering your decisions in the wrong direction.

hot-takes.title: Piece of cake
talkingPoints: Something that is very easy to do.
The exam was a piece of cake after all that studying.
Describe a task that turned out to be a piece of cake, even though you expected it to be hard.

hot-takes.title: Add fuel to the fire
talkingPoints: To make a bad situation, argument, or emotion even worse.
Bringing up old mistakes just added fuel to the fire during our argument.
Share a moment when your words or actions added fuel to the fire in a conflict.

hot-takes.title: A double-edged sword
talkingPoints: Something that has both positive and negative consequences.
Social media is a double-edged sword — it connects us but can also isolate us.
Talk about something in your life that has been a double-edged sword.

hot-takes.title: Put your foot in your mouth
talkingPoints: To say something embarrassing or tactless without meaning to.
I really put my foot in my mouth when I asked if she was pregnant — she wasn't.
Share an embarrassing time you put your foot in your mouth in front of others.

hot-takes.title: Flog a dead horse
talkingPoints: To waste time and effort on something that has no chance of succeeding.
Trying to convince him again is just flogging a dead horse — his mind is made up.
Describe a situation where you kept flogging a dead horse instead of moving on.

hot-takes.title: Don't put the cart before the horse
talkingPoints: Don't do things in the wrong order, especially by handling a later step before an earlier, necessary one.
He started designing the app before defining what problem it would solve — putting the cart before the horse.
Describe a time you put the cart before the horse and had to backtrack.

hot-takes.title: Beauty
talkingPoints: The quality of being pleasing to the senses or the mind.
There was a quiet beauty in the way the fog settled over the hills.
Describe something ordinary that you find surprisingly beautiful.

hot-takes.title: Listening
talkingPoints: The act of giving attention to and trying to understand what someone says.
Sometimes listening quietly did more for her friend than any advice could.
Describe a time when simply listening mattered more than speaking.

hot-takes.title: Nature
talkingPoints: The physical world and everything in it not made by humans.
A weekend in nature helped him reset after a stressful month.
Describe a place in nature that always calms you down.

hot-takes.title: Ocean
talkingPoints: A vast body of salt water covering most of the Earth's surface.
Standing at the edge of the ocean made all her problems feel small.
Talk about how being near the ocean, or water in general, affects you.

hot-takes.title: Vacation
talkingPoints: An extended period of leisure or travel away from work or daily routine.
Their vacation to the mountains ended up being more memorable than any beach trip.
Talk about a vacation that didn't go as planned but turned out great anyway.

hot-takes.title: Resilience
talkingPoints: The capacity to recover quickly from difficulties; toughness.
Her resilience helped her bounce back after losing her job.
Describe a setback you recovered from and what it taught you about your own resilience.

hot-takes.title: Transformation
talkingPoints: A thorough or dramatic change in form, appearance, or character.
The neighborhood's transformation from empty lots to a thriving market took a decade.
Talk about a personal transformation you've gone through and what triggered it.

hot-takes.title: Influence
talkingPoints: The capacity to have an effect on the character or actions of someone or something.
Her early mentor's influence still shapes how she leads meetings today.
Talk about a person whose influence changed the direction of your life.

hot-takes.title: Culture
talkingPoints: The customs, arts, and social behavior of a particular group or society.
The startup's culture of open feedback made even junior employees feel heard.
Describe an aspect of a culture, workplace or otherwise, that shaped who you are.

hot-takes.title: Momentum
talkingPoints: The impetus gained by a process or course of events, driving it forward.
One early win gave the campaign the momentum it needed to keep volunteers energized.
Talk about a project where momentum built up until it felt unstoppable, or died before it started.

hot-takes.title: Recovery
talkingPoints: The process of returning to a normal state of health, mind, or strength.
His recovery from the injury took twice as long as the doctors predicted.
Describe a recovery, physical or otherwise, that taught you something about patience.

hot-takes.title: Polarization
talkingPoints: The process by which opinions or groups split into two sharply opposing extremes.
Political polarization has made it harder for opposing parties to compromise on basic policy.
Discuss whether you think growing polarization in your community or country can still be reversed, and what it would take.

hot-takes.title: Consciousness
talkingPoints: The state of being aware of and able to think about one's own existence, thoughts, and surroundings.
Scientists still debate how physical processes in the brain give rise to consciousness.
Explain why you think consciousness is so hard to explain scientifically, even though we experience it directly every moment.

hot-takes.title: Emancipation
talkingPoints: The act of freeing someone from legal, social, or political restrictions.
The emancipation of enslaved people did not immediately bring full equality.
Discuss a form of emancipation, personal or political, that you believe still needs to happen today.

hot-takes.title: Symbol
talkingPoints: An object, image, or word that represents something else, often an idea or quality.
The dove became a symbol of peace after the war.
Describe an object in your own life that has become a personal symbol of something important to you.

hot-takes.title: Progress
talkingPoints: Forward movement toward a better or more developed state.
The team measured progress not by speed but by the quality of what they built.
Discuss an area of your life where you're unsure whether recent change actually counts as progress.

hot-takes.title: Rationality
talkingPoints: The quality of being based on clear reason and logic rather than emotion.
Economists often assume a level of rationality that doesn't match how people actually behave.
Share a decision where you believed you were being fully rational, but later realized emotion had played a bigger role than you thought.

millennial.title: Bite the bullet
talkingPoints: To force yourself to do something difficult or unpleasant that you have been avoiding.
I hate going to the dentist, but I finally bit the bullet and booked an appointment.
Share a time you had to bite the bullet and face something you'd been putting off.

millennial.title: Burn the midnight oil
talkingPoints: To work late into the night on something.
She burned the midnight oil for a week to finish her thesis on time.
Describe a time you had to burn the midnight oil to meet a deadline.

millennial.title: Burn the candle at both ends
talkingPoints: To work or stay busy from early morning until late at night, exhausting yourself.
Between two jobs and night classes, she was burning the candle at both ends.
Describe a period when you were burning the candle at both ends and how it affected you.

millennial.title: Rain on someone's parade
talkingPoints: To spoil someone's plans or happy mood.
I hate to rain on your parade, but the venue is already booked for that date.
Describe a time someone rained on your parade, or you had to rain on someone else's.

millennial.title: Fly in the face of something
talkingPoints: To clearly contradict or go against something, such as common sense or accepted rules.
His decision to quit without a backup plan flew in the face of everything he'd been taught.
Share a decision you made that flew in the face of others' advice.

millennial.title: Throw caution to the wind
talkingPoints: To act boldly without worrying about the risk or consequences.
She threw caution to the wind and quit her stable job to travel the world.
Talk about a time you threw caution to the wind and took a big risk.

millennial.title: Health
talkingPoints: The state of being free from illness and physically or mentally well.
He changed his diet after his health scare last year.
Talk about a change you made that improved your health, physical or mental.

millennial.title: Understanding
talkingPoints: Sympathetic awareness or comprehension of another person's situation or feelings.
It took real understanding for him to see his sister's side of things.
Talk about a moment you finally understood someone after seeing things their way.

millennial.title: Time
talkingPoints: The ongoing progression of existence measured in moments, hours, and years.
She realized too late how little time she'd spent with her grandfather.
Talk about how your relationship with time has changed as you've gotten older.

millennial.title: Mountain
talkingPoints: A large natural elevation of the earth's surface rising abruptly from the surrounding level.
Reaching the top of the mountain felt like conquering more than just the trail.
Describe a 'mountain,' literal or figurative, that you're proud of climbing.

millennial.title: Celebration
talkingPoints: A social gathering or activity organized to mark a special occasion.
The whole street joined the celebration when the local team won.
Describe a celebration that felt especially meaningful to you.

millennial.title: Perseverance
talkingPoints: Steady persistence in a course of action despite difficulty or delay in achieving success.
His perseverance through years of rejection finally paid off when his novel was published.
Talk about a goal you almost quit on and the moment you decided to keep going.

millennial.title: Evolution
talkingPoints: The gradual development of something from a simpler to a more complex state.
The evolution of her career from intern to director happened one small risk at a time.
Describe how your thinking on something important has evolved over the years.

millennial.title: Connection
talkingPoints: A relationship in which people are linked or associated with each other.
A single honest conversation on a long flight turned into a lifelong connection.
Describe an unexpected connection you made with someone that turned into something meaningful.

millennial.title: Tradition
talkingPoints: A long-established custom or belief passed down within a group.
Every Sunday dinner tradition in her family started with someone telling a story.
Talk about a tradition you've kept alive and one you've chosen to let go.

millennial.title: Stagnation
talkingPoints: A state of little or no growth or development.
The company slid into stagnation once it stopped investing in new ideas.
Describe a period of stagnation in your life and what eventually broke you out of it.

millennial.title: Renewal
talkingPoints: The action of resuming or reinstating something after a break; a fresh start.
A week completely offline gave her the sense of renewal she'd been missing for months.
Talk about a moment of renewal in your life, when you felt like you were starting over.

millennial.title: Reconciliation
talkingPoints: The restoring of a friendly relationship after conflict or disagreement.
The two nations pursued reconciliation decades after the war had ended.
Talk about a relationship in your own life that needed reconciliation, and what made forgiveness possible or impossible.

millennial.title: Ideology
talkingPoints: A structured set of beliefs and values that shapes how a person or group interprets the world and forms political goals.
The party's ideology shaped every policy it proposed, from taxation to education.
Reflect on how much of your own worldview you chose deliberately versus absorbed from the ideology around you growing up.

millennial.title: Oppression
talkingPoints: The unjust or cruel exercise of power over a group of people.
The novel depicts a community's long struggle against political oppression.
Talk about a form of oppression you've witnessed or studied, and what you think ordinary people can do about it.

millennial.title: Myth
talkingPoints: A traditional story, often explaining a natural or social phenomenon, that a culture holds to carry deeper truth even if not literally factual.
The myth of the self-made billionaire ignores the role of luck and privilege.
Pick a widely believed myth in your culture or industry and explain why you think it persists despite evidence against it.

millennial.title: Regression
talkingPoints: A return to a former, typically less advanced or developed, state.
After the injury, his recovery hit a regression that frustrated everyone on the medical team.
Describe a time you experienced a regression after making real progress, and how you responded to the setback.

millennial.title: Irrationality
talkingPoints: Behavior or thinking that is not based on logic or clear reasoning.
Panic buying during the shortage was a clear case of collective irrationality.
Describe an irrational fear or habit you have, and explain why logic alone hasn't been enough to change it.

gen-z.title: The tip of the iceberg
talkingPoints: A small, visible part of a much larger problem or situation.
The errors we found in the report were just the tip of the iceberg.
Describe a problem in your life that turned out to be just the tip of the iceberg.

gen-z.title: Caught between a rock and a hard place
talkingPoints: Faced with two difficult choices, neither of which is good.
He was caught between a rock and a hard place: disappoint his boss or miss his daughter's recital.
Talk about a time you felt caught between a rock and a hard place.

gen-z.title: The writing is on the wall
talkingPoints: There are clear signs that something bad or a failure is going to happen.
When sales kept dropping every month, the writing was on the wall for the store's closure.
Share a time you saw the writing on the wall before something ended or changed.

gen-z.title: Rub someone the wrong way
talkingPoints: To irritate or annoy someone, often unintentionally.
His constant interrupting really rubs me the wrong way.
Talk about a habit or behavior that rubs you the wrong way.

gen-z.title: A fool and his money are soon parted
talkingPoints: A saying meaning that people who spend carelessly quickly lose their money.
He bought three lottery tickets a day — a fool and his money are soon parted.
Describe a purchase you regretted that made you think of the saying a fool and his money are soon parted.

gen-z.title: Courage
talkingPoints: The ability to do something that frightens you; mental or moral strength to face difficulty.
It took real courage for her to speak up in the meeting.
Talk about a moment you had to find courage to do something that scared you.

gen-z.title: Friendship
talkingPoints: A close relationship of mutual affection and trust between people.
Their friendship survived twenty years and three different countries.
Describe a friendship that has shaped who you are today.

gen-z.title: Forgiveness
talkingPoints: The act of pardoning someone for a mistake or wrongdoing.
Forgiveness didn't come easily, but it freed her from years of anger.
Share a time you forgave someone, or were forgiven, and what it changed.

gen-z.title: Memory
talkingPoints: The faculty of retaining and recalling past experiences, or a specific recollection.
The smell of fresh bread always brings back a memory of her childhood kitchen.
Share a memory that still feels vivid no matter how much time has passed.

gen-z.title: Journey
talkingPoints: An act of traveling from one place to another, or a long process of change.
Her journey to recovery took far longer than she expected.
Talk about a journey, literal or personal, that changed how you see yourself.

gen-z.title: Tradition
talkingPoints: A custom or belief passed down through generations.
Their Sunday dinner tradition never once broke, even during hard years.
Talk about a family or cultural tradition you hope to keep passing on.

gen-z.title: Adaptability
talkingPoints: The quality of being able to adjust to new conditions.
The team's adaptability let them pivot their strategy overnight when the market shifted.
Share a time your plans fell apart and describe how you adapted on the spot.

gen-z.title: Progress
talkingPoints: Forward or onward movement toward a destination or goal.
Progress on the project was slow, but every small win kept the team motivated.
Share a goal where you had to measure progress in small steps instead of big leaps.

gen-z.title: Communication
talkingPoints: The imparting or exchanging of information or ideas.
Better communication between the two teams cut the project delays in half.
Share a time a misunderstanding taught you something about how you communicate.

gen-z.title: Modernity
talkingPoints: The quality of being current or contemporary, especially as contrasted with tradition.
The city's rush toward modernity left little room for its old markets to survive.
Describe a moment when modernity and tradition collided in your own life.

gen-z.title: Mentorship
talkingPoints: Guidance and support provided by a more experienced or knowledgeable person.
Her mentorship of younger engineers became just as rewarding as her own coding work.
Talk about a mentor who changed your path, or a time you mentored someone else.

gen-z.title: Routine
talkingPoints: A sequence of actions regularly followed; a fixed program.
A simple morning routine was the one thing that kept her grounded during a chaotic year.
Describe a routine that has quietly shaped your life for the better or worse.

gen-z.title: Pragmatism
talkingPoints: An approach that judges ideas and actions by their practical consequences rather than abstract theory.
Her pragmatism led her to choose the imperfect solution that actually worked over the ideal one that didn't.
Argue for or against the idea that pragmatism should always win out over principle when the two conflict.

gen-z.title: Hegemony
talkingPoints: Dominance of one group, nation, or set of ideas over others, often exercised through influence rather than force.
Historians study how economic hegemony can shape global politics without a single shot being fired.
Discuss an example of cultural or economic hegemony you've noticed in your own life, and how it shapes what people consider normal.

gen-z.title: Resistance
talkingPoints: The act of opposing or fighting against something, especially an authority or force.
The underground newspaper became a symbol of resistance during the occupation.
Describe a time you resisted pressure to go along with something you thought was wrong.

gen-z.title: Ritual
talkingPoints: A set sequence of actions performed regularly, often carrying symbolic or ceremonial meaning.
The morning coffee ritual gave her a sense of calm before the workday began.
Describe a personal ritual that matters to you and explain what would be lost if you had to give it up.

gen-z.title: Entropy
talkingPoints: A tendency toward increasing disorder or decline in a system over time.
Without regular maintenance, the old machine slowly succumbed to entropy.
Discuss an area of your life, like a relationship or a project, where you've had to actively fight entropy to keep it from falling apart.

gen-z.title: Bias
talkingPoints: A tendency to favor one perspective, group, or outcome, often unconsciously, over an objective assessment.
The hiring panel trained to recognize their own unconscious bias before reviewing applications.
Identify a bias you've caught yourself acting on, and describe what helped you notice it.

eli5.title: Actions speak louder than words
talkingPoints: What people actually do matters more than what they say they will do.
He kept promising to help, but actions speak louder than words, and he never showed up.
Talk about a person in your life whose actions really did speak louder than words.

eli5.title: Don't put all your eggs in one basket
talkingPoints: You shouldn't risk everything on a single plan or option.
She applied to five universities because you shouldn't put all your eggs in one basket.
Describe a decision where you either followed or ignored the advice not to put all your eggs in one basket.

eli5.title: Blow hot and cold
talkingPoints: To keep changing your opinion or attitude about something, being inconsistent.
He keeps blowing hot and cold about whether he wants the promotion.
Describe a time you blew hot and cold about a decision before finally committing.

eli5.title: Shoot yourself in the foot
talkingPoints: To do something that unintentionally makes your own situation worse.
By insulting the interviewer, he shot himself in the foot before the job even started.
Describe a time you shot yourself in the foot by making things worse for yourself.

eli5.title: Sour grapes
talkingPoints: Pretending not to want something after failing to get it, out of bitterness.
He said he never wanted the promotion anyway, but everyone knew it was just sour grapes.
Talk about a time you or someone you know reacted to disappointment with sour grapes.

eli5.title: Patience
talkingPoints: The capacity to accept or tolerate delay, trouble, or suffering without becoming annoyed.
He waited in line for two hours without losing his patience.
Describe a situation that tested your patience and how you got through it.

eli5.title: Family
talkingPoints: A group of people related by blood, marriage, or close bonds.
Family gathered from across the country for the reunion.
Talk about a tradition your family has that means a lot to you.

eli5.title: Gratitude
talkingPoints: The quality of being thankful and appreciative.
Keeping a gratitude journal changed the way he saw his daily life.
Talk about something small you're grateful for that most people overlook.

eli5.title: Habit
talkingPoints: A regular practice or routine, especially one that is hard to give up.
Checking his phone first thing every morning became a hard habit to break.
Describe a habit you've tried to change and how that's going.

eli5.title: Adventure
talkingPoints: An unusual, exciting, or daring experience.
Quitting his job to backpack alone was the adventure of his life.
Describe an adventure you took, or one you still want to take.

eli5.title: Gift
talkingPoints: A thing given willingly without payment, often to show affection or appreciation.
The handmade gift meant more to her than anything store-bought ever could.
Share the story behind a gift you gave or received that really stuck with you.

eli5.title: Integrity
talkingPoints: The quality of being honest and having strong moral principles.
She refused to fudge the numbers, choosing integrity over an easy shortcut.
Describe a moment when doing the right thing cost you something, and why you did it anyway.

eli5.title: Stagnation
talkingPoints: A state of little or no growth or development.
Years of stagnation in the same role finally pushed her to ask for a new challenge.
Talk about a time you felt stuck and what finally got you moving again.

eli5.title: Collaboration
talkingPoints: The action of working with someone to produce or create something.
The mural was the product of a collaboration between six different artists.
Talk about a project that only worked because of real collaboration, not solo effort.

eli5.title: History
talkingPoints: The study of past events, or the record of what has happened over time.
Knowing the neighborhood's history changed how she saw every building on the block.
Talk about a piece of history, personal or shared, that changed how you see the present.

eli5.title: Rivalry
talkingPoints: A state or situation of competing with someone for the same objective.
The friendly rivalry between the two siblings pushed both of them to train harder.
Describe a rivalry, friendly or otherwise, that pushed you to improve.

eli5.title: Spontaneity
talkingPoints: The quality of being done or occurring without planning.
A spontaneity that used to scare him became the thing he loved most about traveling.
Talk about a spontaneous decision that turned into one of your favorite memories.

eli5.title: Stoicism
talkingPoints: An ancient philosophy that teaches maintaining calm and rational acceptance in the face of hardship.
He practiced stoicism by refusing to let the delayed flight ruin his mood.
Reflect on whether stoicism helps you cope with setbacks or whether it sometimes stops you from processing emotions honestly.

eli5.title: Paradox
talkingPoints: A statement or situation that seems to contradict itself yet may still be true.
It's a paradox that the more choices we have, the less satisfied we often feel with our decisions.
Share a paradox you've noticed in your own life or field, and try to explain how both sides of it can be true at once.

eli5.title: Solidarity
talkingPoints: Unity and mutual support among people who share common interests or goals.
Workers across the city showed solidarity by joining the strike even though it wasn't their own factory.
Share an experience where showing solidarity with someone else's cause cost you something, and whether it was worth it.

eli5.title: Identity
talkingPoints: The set of characteristics, beliefs, and experiences that define who a person is.
Moving to a new country forced him to reconsider parts of his own identity.
Talk about a part of your identity that has shifted significantly over the years, and what caused the change.

eli5.title: Complexity
talkingPoints: The state of having many interconnected parts, making something difficult to fully understand or predict.
The complexity of the supply chain meant one small delay could ripple across the whole company.
Talk about a problem you once thought was simple but discovered had far more complexity than you expected.

eli5.title: Empathy
talkingPoints: The ability to understand and share the feelings of another person.
Her empathy for the new employee helped her remember what it was like to feel lost on the first day.
Describe a time someone's empathy toward you changed how you felt about a difficult situation.
